about: The Ultimate Challenge's own rounds: never played on the Board or in Defuse. Cambridge formats only, written around the traps B2 First actually sets.

rounds.prompt: The girl ___ bag was stolen went to the police.
rounds.note: whose: possession (her bag).

rounds.prompt: That's the café ___ we first met.
rounds.note: where for a place in a relative clause.

rounds.prompt: ___ of my friends like horror films, so I watch them alone.
rounds.note: None of + plural: not one.

rounds.prompt: There's ___ milk left. Can you buy some?
rounds.note: hardly any + uncountable: almost none.

rounds.prompt: ___ I need right now is a long holiday.
rounds.note: What I need is … : a cleft sentence for emphasis.

rounds.prompt: It was ___ a boring lesson that I fell asleep.
rounds.note: such a + adjective + noun + that.

rounds.prompt: The exam was ___ difficult that nobody finished.
rounds.note: so + adjective + that.

rounds.prompt: My brother, ___ lives in London, is coming to visit.
rounds.note: Non-defining clause (with commas): who, never that.

rounds.prompt: Both of the answers ___ correct.
rounds.note: both: always plural.

rounds.prompt: I bought two T-shirts, but ___ of them fits me.
rounds.note: neither of two + singular verb: not one of the two.

rounds.prompt: It was Maria ___ told me the news.
rounds.note: It was + person + who …: a cleft sentence.

rounds.prompt: Each of the students ___ a certificate.
rounds.note: each of + plural noun + singular verb.

rounds.prompt: She gave me ___ advice.
rounds.note: advice is uncountable: some advice, never an advice.

rounds.prompt: There were ___ people at the party that we ran out of food.
rounds.note: so many + plural noun + that.

rounds.prompt: This is the book ___ I told you about.
rounds.note: that / which for things in a defining clause; never what.

rounds.prompt: ___ students in the class passed; not a single one failed.
rounds.note: All the + plural; every and each take a singular noun.

rounds.prompt: The man ___ car I scratched was very angry.
rounds.note: whose + noun: possession.

rounds.prompt: This is the town ___ I was born.
rounds.note: where for a place.

rounds.prompt: ___ of the two films was any good.
rounds.note: Neither of the two: not one or the other.

rounds.prompt: What I love about summer ___ the long evenings.
rounds.note: What … is: the cleft takes is (are is also heard before a plural).

rounds.prompt: It was ___ a lovely day that we went to the beach.
rounds.note: such a + adjective + noun + that.

rounds.prompt: There isn't ___ bread left.
rounds.note: any / much in a negative with an uncountable noun.

rounds.prompt: I have two brothers, ___ of whom are older than me.
rounds.note: both of whom: the two of them.

rounds.prompt: She has very ___ friends at her new school, so she feels lonely.
rounds.note: very few + plural: almost none.

rounds.prompt: The reason ___ I'm calling is to say thank you.
rounds.note: the reason why / that.

rounds.prompt: ___ was my brother who broke the vase.
rounds.note: It was … who …: a cleft sentence.

rounds.prompt: Is ___ anything I can do to help?
rounds.note: Is there anything …?

rounds.prompt: He plays ___ guitar in a band.
rounds.note: play the + instrument.

rounds.prompt: They've helped each ___ a lot this year.
rounds.note: each other: two people, both ways.

rounds.prompt: ___ is the best day of the week to visit?
rounds.note: Which / What for a question about one of a set.

rounds.prompt: I only need a cup of coffee.
rounds.note: All I need is … = I only need …

rounds.prompt: My friend lives in that house.
rounds.note: where + clause for a place.

rounds.prompt: The weather was so bad that we cancelled the trip.
rounds.stem: It was ___ that we cancelled the trip.
rounds.note: so + adjective = such + adjective + noun (weather is uncountable: no a).

rounds.prompt: Her father is a doctor. She is the girl.
rounds.stem: She is the girl ___ a doctor.
rounds.note: whose for possession.

rounds.prompt: None of the students passed the test.
rounds.note: none passed = all failed.

rounds.prompt: There's very little sugar in the cupboard.
rounds.note: very little = hardly any.

rounds.prompt: Ana told me the truth, not Rui.
rounds.stem: It was Ana ___ the truth, not Rui.
rounds.note: It was + person + who …

rounds.prompt: I don't like either of these jackets.
rounds.note: not … either = neither.

rounds.prompt: The book was so interesting that I couldn't stop reading.
rounds.stem: It was ___ book that I couldn't stop reading.
rounds.note: so + adjective = such a(n) + adjective + noun.

rounds.prompt: I really want a new bike.
rounds.note: What I want is … : a cleft for emphasis.

rounds.prompt: Not many people came to the meeting.
rounds.note: not many = few.

rounds.prompt: We stayed at a hotel. The hotel was lovely.
rounds.note: which for things; the preposition can go at the end or before which.

rounds.prompt: There were too many people for us to get in.
rounds.stem: There were ___ that we couldn't get in.
rounds.note: so many + plural noun + that.

rounds.prompt: Every student received a prize.
rounds.note: each = every, with a singular verb.

rounds.prompt: I admire him more than anyone else.
rounds.note: the one I admire most = the person I admire more than anyone.

rounds.prompt: I have no money left at all.
rounds.note: no = not any.
